sub_answers.text: Rare local subtree-pattern counts in large critical Bienaym\'e--Galton--Watson trees are asymptotically Poisson in total variation when marked fringe subtrees remain microscopic and nearby marked occurrences have negligible clustering and the mean stays bounded [d127320s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which conjectures or open problems relate the Wiener index to subtree counts or other structural invariants in binary trees?
What limitations arise when extending extremal results from rooted binary trees to unrooted or non-binary trees?
sub_answers.text: No maximum agreement forest (MAF) formulation is known for unrooted SPR distance and four properties of optimal SPR paths suggest that no MAF formulation exists in the unrooted case [d30106s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In which algorithms does the Wiener index or pairwise distance sum of a tree play a critical role (e.g., phylogenetics, network routing)?
sub_answers.text: The Wiener index is defined as the sum of distances between all pairs of vertices of a graph and is a widely used topological index [d93723s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are subtree counts used in computational problems such as pattern matching, motif counting, or enumeration of rooted substructures?
sub_answers.text: Largest common subtree and smallest common supertree problems use subtree relations to compute tree similarity and can be transformed into one another by linear-time constructions [d140435s0p0].

sub_answers.text: Cache-oblivious B-tree-like structures support inserting and removing a subtree with explicit amortized I/O and time complexity bounds that scale with the subtree size and tree parameters [d79299s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are bounds relating distances and subtree counts applied in graph drawing, chemical graph theory, or combinatorial enumeration?
sub_answers.text: Extremal bounds on the Wiener index under diameter constraints are used to characterize graphs that maximize pairwise distance sums, which informs chemical graph-theoretic topological index studies and extremal enumeration [d93723s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is the definition of a binary tree in graph-theoretic terms, including rooted and ordered variants?
sub_answers.text:
A rooted binary phylogenetic tree is a rooted tree whose leaf set X represents a set of species and whose edges have real-valued lengths (weights) [d68950s0p0].
A k-caterpillar is a binary tree consisting of a path with smaller j-caterpillars (0 ≤ j ≤ k−1) attached to some vertices on the path, and a 0-caterpillar is a path [d71028s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How is the sum of distances between all pairs of vertices in a tree (Wiener index) defined and computed?
sub_answers.text:
The Wiener index W(G) of a graph G is defined as the sum of distances between all unordered pairs of vertices of G [d93723s0p0].
The Wiener index is computed by summing the pairwise distances between every two vertices in the graph [d57043s0p0].
The diameter D(G) is the maximum distance between all pairs of vertices, and conditional diameter generalizes this to vertex subsets of fixed cardinality [d93723s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What constitutes a subtree in a rooted binary tree, and how is the number of subtrees formally counted?
sub_answers.text:
For a subset S of leaves in a rooted phylogenetic tree, the minimal subtree connecting the species in S is the union of edges required to connect those leaves in the tree [d68950s0p0].
A fringe subtree is a local subtree used to specify a pattern by marks on fringe subtrees in conditioned Bienaymé–Galton–Watson trees [d127320s0p0].
Counts of such marked fringe subtrees or of occurrences of specified subtree patterns are used to enumerate subtrees and study their distribution in random trees [d127320s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are common classes of binary trees (e.g., full, complete, path-like, balanced) used in extremal combinatorics?
sub_answers.text:
Path-star trees are formed by taking a path and attaching g pendant vertices to one end vertex and are used as extremal examples in distance problems on trees [d35580s0p0].
k-caterpillars and 0-caterpillars (paths) are classes of binary trees built by attaching smaller caterpillars to a central path and are studied in embedding and extremal problems [d71028s0p0].
Perfectly balanced k-caterpillars are those k-caterpillars that contain a perfect matching and are considered in spanning and embedding conjectures for hypercubes [d71028s0p0].
Rooted binary normal networks and rooted binary phylogenetic trees are distinguished classes in phylogenetics used to study reconstructibility from small subtree patterns such as caterpillars on three and four leaves [d56253s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does one compute the Wiener index incrementally using edge contributions or subtree sizes in a tree?
What combinatorial identities express the number of subtrees of a rooted binary tree in terms of node degrees or child-subtree sizes?
sub_answers.text: Counts of marked fringe subtrees in size-conditioned Bienaymé--Galton--Watson trees are asymptotically Poisson in total variation when the marked fringe subtrees remain microscopic and nearby marked occurrences have negligible clustering [d127320s0p0]. When the mean count of such marked fringe subtrees diverges, their count satisfies a law of large numbers [d127320s0p0]. For non-fringe patterns, overlapping occurrences may form clusters and the raw count need not be asymptotically Poisson, so declumped indicators selecting boundary witnesses of clusters are used to obtain Poisson approximations [d127320s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which tree transformations (pruning, rotation, grafting, contraction) change distance sums and subtree counts, and how are their effects quantified?
sub_answers.text: Pruning decisions that include or exclude whole subtrees can be derived from node metadata and symbolic interval analysis, enabling efficient subtree pruning or inclusion in tree traversals [d116209s0p0]. Subtree substitution treats subtrees with similar semantic functions as exchangeable and is used for compositional data augmentation by swapping subtrees [d75903s0p0]. Linear-time constructions transform a smallest common supertree into a largest common subtree and vice versa for isomorphic, homeomorphic, topological, and minor embeddings, providing algebraic conversions between common-super and common-sub structures [d140435s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What known extremal constructions (e.g., path, complete binary tree, caterpillar, star-like) achieve maxima or minima for distance sums or subtree counts?
sub_answers.text: Path-star trees P_{n-g,g}, obtained by adding g pendant vertices to one end of a path on n-g vertices, maximize the distance between center and subtree core and between centroid and subtree core among trees on n vertices for appropriate g, and some path-star tree P_{n-g_0,g_0} attains the maximum among path-star trees where g_0 is the smallest positive integer with 2^{g_0}+g_0>n-1 [d35580s0p0]. Perfectly balanced 2-caterpillars are notable extremal trees that span hypercubes of appropriate dimension and serve as structured extremal constructions in binary-tree embedding problems [d71028s0p0]. Complete r-ary subtree patterns (for r ≥ 1) are significant extremal local patterns whose heights and occurrences are localized in conditioned Bienaymé trees and figure in maximum-pattern asymptotics [d127320s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For n-node binary trees, what are the strongest proven upper and lower bounds (exact formulas, constant factors, and leading asymptotic terms) on the total number of distinct subtrees; which constructions attain or approach these bounds, and what ranges of n or families of binary trees still lack matching upper and lower bounds?
sub_answers.text: Counts of rare local patterns in size-conditioned critical Bienaymé–Galton–Watson trees satisfy Poisson approximation in total variation when the mean remains bounded, and satisfy a law of large numbers when the mean diverges [d127320s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What conjectures, published hypotheses, or open problems propose relationships between the Wiener index (sum of all pairwise distances) and the number of subtrees or other quantitative invariants (e.g., subtree distribution, degree sequence, path count, eccentricity) in binary trees, and what partial results or counterexamples are known for these conjectures?
sub_answers.text: Fano's lower bound is exact for the relation diagram of 'Error Probability vs. Conditional Entropy' for binary classifications, and a new upper bound for the Bayesian error is derived with respect to the minimum prior probability [d17947s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: When attempting to transfer extremal theorems about subtree counts or related measures from rooted full/plane binary trees to unrooted binary trees, general (non-binary) trees, or trees with higher maximum degree, what counterexamples, structural obstacles, or changes in extremal configurations have been documented, and which aspects of the proofs fail or require new techniques?
sub_answers.text: Overlapping occurrences of non-fringe patterns can form clusters that prevent raw counts from being asymptotically Poisson, necessitating declumped indicators and new techniques to select boundary witnesses of clusters [d127320s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the known algorithmic hardness results and complexity-theoretic barriers for computing maximum or minimum values of subtree counts, Wiener index, or other extremal tree metrics; what is known about the complexity of certifying optimality (e.g., NP-hardness, #P-hardness, fixed-parameter tractability, approximation thresholds) and which specific decision or optimization variants remain open?
sub_answers.text: A polynomial-time algorithm is given to compute non-trivial lower bounds on the tangle crossing number in O(n^4) time, and this lower bound may be tight even for tanglegrams with tangle crossing number Θ(n^2) [d39960s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which algorithms and computational fields explicitly use the Wiener index (sum of all pairwise distances in a tree) as a core metric or optimization objective — for instance: phylogenetic tree reconstruction methods, network routing cost models, facility location on trees, or tree-shaped clustering algorithms?

In what algorithmic contexts are counts of subtrees or rooted-subtree occurrences directly computed or exploited — for example in string/tree pattern matching, counting network motifs, dynamic programming for subtree isomorphism, frequent subtree mining, or enumerating rooted induced subtrees for probabilistic models?
sub_answers.text:
Largest-common-subtree and smallest-common-supertree constructions are used in tree pattern matching and can be obtained from one another in linear time [d140435s0p0].
Counts of rare local subtree patterns are directly analyzed and approximated by Poisson laws in conditioned Bienaymé trees for probabilistic models [d127320s0p0].
An algorithm computes the largest subtree in local Bruhat–Tits trees from generators of a suborder, which is an explicit exploitation of subtree structure [d23840s0p0].
Quantitative analysis of attack trees computes security metrics that rely on subtree structures and shared subtrees in attack-graph models [d67456s0p0][d81577s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the consequences of extremal tree topologies (paths, stars, balanced vs. skewed trees) for the worst-case and average-case performance of fundamental data structures and algorithms — including binary search trees, heap-ordered trees, tries, and tree-based indexing structures?
sub_answers.text:
Path-star trees maximize the distance between the center and the subtree core among all trees on n vertices, showing that extremal path-like versus star-like shapes drive worst-case distance measures [d35580s0p0].
Partitioning terminal nodes using the Fiedler vector of a Laplacian produces splits consistent with tree structure and simplifies merging in divide-and-conquer recovery, improving runtime for large latent-tree inference [d65499s0p0].
Asymptotic bounds on diameters of spaces under rearrangement operations show that extremal topologies influence the metric diameter and connectivity properties of tree and network search spaces [d51414s0p0].
Geodesic combinatorics in tree space depend on endpoint locations within a polyhedral subdivision, so extreme placements affect convergence and complexity of Frechet-mean algorithms on tree-shaped data [d16910s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are inequalities that relate distance-based metrics (like the Wiener index or diameter) and subtree-count statistics used in practice — for example in chemical graph theory for predicting molecular properties, in algorithms for planar/tree drawing aesthetics, or in combinatorial proofs/enumeration of labeled/unlabeled trees?
sub_answers.text:
Algebraic constructions relate largest common subtrees and smallest common supertrees, allowing conversions between subtree-combinatorial and embedding problems that use distance-like information [d140435s0p0].
Using subtree-weight estimates in a generalized neighbor-joining transformation demonstrates that combining subtree-count or subtree-weight statistics with pairwise distances can improve distance-based tree reconstruction algorithms [d149070s0p0].
Poisson approximations for counts of marked fringe subtrees provide probabilistic tools linking occurrence counts of small subtree patterns to asymptotic enumeration and statistical inference on large random trees [d127320s0p0].
Accounting for branch lengths (a distance-based metric) when testing tree containment in networks can sharpen localization of trees in networks but may lead to computational hardness in general formulations [d33464s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give a graph-theoretic definition of a binary tree: describe it as an acyclic connected graph with degree constraints, and distinguish the formal definitions of a rooted binary tree and an ordered (plane) binary tree, including parent/child relations and left/right ordering.
sub_answers.text: A tree is a connected graph in which distances between vertices are studied and applications include extremal values of distance-based invariants [d57043s0p0]. A rooted binary tree is a rooted tree in which each non-leaf vertex has at most two children and parent/child relations are defined with respect to the designated root, as in rooted binary phylogenetic and rooted binary rooted-tree contexts [d56253s0p0][d43505s0p0]. A binary tree used for random-walk or traversal models is described by a root, internal vertices that have a parent and up to two children, and leaves with no children, with the root choosing among children as specified by the process [d101730s0p0]. An ordered (plane) binary tree distinguishes left and right children and embedding/order matters when mapping the tree into a planar point set or polygon for point-set embeddings [d17405s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain the Wiener index for trees: provide the formula for the sum of distances over all unordered vertex pairs, discuss alternative expressions (e.g., sums over edges or contributions of edges), and outline standard algorithms or formulas to compute it for a tree.
sub_answers.text: The Wiener index of a connected graph is the sum of the distances between all unordered pairs of vertices [d57043s0p0]. For a tree, the Wiener index is computed by summing dist(u,v) over every unordered vertex pair {u,v} in the vertex set, which is the standard formula used for trees and other connected graphs [d57043s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Precisely define what is meant by a subtree of a rooted binary tree in combinatorics: clarify whether subtrees must be induced, rooted at some node, or contiguous descendants, and give exact counting conventions and formulas used to count all such subtrees.
sub_answers.text: In tree-pattern problems, a subtree may be considered under several embedding notions such as isomorphic, homeomorphic, topological, and minor embeddings, and constructions relate largest common subtrees to smallest common supertrees under these embeddings [d140435s0p0]. In rooted binary phylogenetic contexts, a subtree is often considered as a displayed rooted subnetwork or a displayed rooted triple or caterpillar, meaning the subtree is rooted at some node and consists of descendants arranged according to the rooting of the original tree [d56253s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List and formally define the standard classes of binary trees studied in extremal combinatorics (examples: full/strict/full binary, complete, perfect, path-like/degenerate, balanced/AVL/height-restricted, plane versus nonplane), noting the structural constraints and parameters that distinguish them.
sub_answers.text: A complete binary tree is a complete binary tree structure with specialized local parent-child-sister hierarchies introduced for leaves and nodes to improve memory and performance in complete-binary-tree-based algorithms [d21748s0p0]. A balanced binary tree is a binary tree with structural constraints used for point-set planar embeddings and is treated as a special focus in embedding algorithms for bounded point sets [d17405s0p0]. A rooted binary phylogenetic tree is a rooted binary tree used in phylogenetics and is determined by its displayed rooted triples in the classical setting of rooted binary phylogenetic trees [d56253s0p0]. A path-like or path-star tree is formed by adding pendant vertices to a path to create path-star trees and is used in studies of tree center, centroid, and subtree core properties [d35580s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What formulas express the Wiener index of a tree as a sum of contributions per edge (e.g. for edge e splitting the tree into components of sizes s and n−s, contribution s(n−s)), and how can that be implemented incrementally or updated after a single edge insertion/deletion using subtree sizes or rerooting techniques?

Which exact combinatorial recurrences or closed-form identities count all subtrees of a rooted binary tree in terms of child-subtree sizes or local degree data (for example: formulas for the number of subtrees containing the root, the number of subtrees rooted at a given node, product/sum identities over children, and generating-function descriptions relating node-level quantities to the total subtree count)?

For basic tree operations—removing a leaf (pruning), rotating a subtree, grafting a subtree to a different parent, and contracting an edge—what are the explicit delta formulas for (a) the Wiener index and (b) the total number of subtrees, expressed in terms of sizes of the affected subtrees/components and local degree changes?

For fixed n, which explicit tree families (path, star, balanced complete binary tree, complete k-ary tree, caterpillar, broom/star-caterpillar hybrids) are known to maximize or minimize the Wiener index or the total number of subtrees, and what are the precise extremal values or inequalities (including known threshold n ranges and proof references) for each objective?

Survey tight upper and lower bounds (exact formulas, constant factors, and leading asymptotic terms) known for the maximum and minimum number of distinct subtrees in binary trees with n internal nodes or n leaves; identify ranges of n or classes of binary trees where only coarse bounds are known and list the precise open gaps in asymptotic behavior or multiplicative/additive constants.
sub_answers.text:
Counts of rare local subtree patterns in size-conditioned critical Bienaym\'e--Galton--Watson trees obey a Poisson approximation in total variation whenever their mean remains bounded [d127320s0p0].
When the mean of such subtree counts diverges, the counts satisfy a law of large numbers [d127320s0p0].
Heights of the largest complete r-ary subtrees (for r\u22652) are localized on one or two consecutive integers under the same model [d127320s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Catalog conjectures, published open problems, and partial results that link the Wiener index (sum of all pairwise distances) to subtree counts or to other structural invariants (e.g., number of leaves, imbalance measures, path-length, subtree frequency spectra) for binary trees; include named conjectures, authors, provenance (papers/years), and any counterexamples or supporting computational evidence.
sub_answers.text:
A corrected Ordered Leaf Attachment (OLA) distance index corresponds to the size of a maximum acyclic agreement forest (MAAF) given an optimal leaf ordering, and this distance is computable in linear time [d113586s0p0].
A MAAF can be reconstructed from optimal OLA vectors, enabling identification of reticulation events under an optimal leaf ordering [d113586s0p0].
Algorithms exist that optimally resolve multifurcated trees given a leaf-ordering in time O(kn\u22c5 m log m), where m is the size of the largest multifurcation [d113586s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain which proof techniques, counterexamples, or structural transformations prevent direct extension of extremal theorems proved for rooted binary trees (e.g., maximum/minimum subtree count, extremal Wiener index) to unrooted trees or to trees with maximum degree > 2; specify which properties fail (symmetry, rooting-based recurrence, leaf-count preservation) and give concrete examples illustrating the limitations.
sub_answers.text:
For unrooted binary trees, shortest NNI-walks that visit all trees in an SPR neighborhood take \u03b8(n^2) additional steps beyond the number of trees in that SPR neighborhood, indicating structural differences in neighborhood traversal between rooted and unrooted settings [d12536s0p0].
Algebraic constructions that transform between largest common subtrees and smallest common supertrees work uniformly across isomorphic, homeomorphic, topological, and minor embeddings and run in linear time, showing that some rooting-dependent recurrences can be bypassed by embedding-preserving constructions [d140435s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List known NP-hardness, #P-hardness, fixed-parameter tractability, approximation hardness results, or provable certificate-size lower bounds for computing extremal combinatorial values (maximum/minimum subtree count, extremal Wiener index, extremal structural invariants) on trees; indicate which decision/optimization problems are hard, the reductions used, and whether optimality can be certified in polynomial time for restricted families (bounded degree, bounded height).
sub_answers.text:
The corrected OLA distance between k trees is computable in linear time and yields a MAAF when an optimal leaf ordering is given, so reconstruction of the corresponding MAAF is polynomial-time in that setting [d113586s0p0].
There is an O(kn\u22c5 m log m) algorithm that optimally resolves multifurcated trees given a leaf-ordering, with m the size of the largest multifurcation, providing fixed-parameter polynomial-time solvability when m is bounded [d113586s0p0].
Improvements to maximum-weight bipartite matching algorithms are possible when input graphs are node-unbalanced or weight-unbalanced, and these enhancements underpin faster maximum agreement subtree algorithms [d140232s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which algorithms and application domains rely explicitly on the Wiener index or the sum of all pairwise distances in a tree—for example, algorithms in evolutionary tree reconstruction, distance-based clustering, routing cost optimization in communication networks, or graph kernel methods—and how is that metric used within those algorithms?

In which algorithmic tasks are counts of rooted or unrooted subtrees (or occurrences of small tree motifs) computed or estimated—such as string/structure pattern matching, frequent subtree mining, RNA secondary-structure enumeration, or counting induced subtrees in parameterized algorithms—and what exact role do those subtree counts play in the computation or complexity analysis?
sub_answers.text:
Constructions between largest common subtree and smallest common supertree connect two tree pattern matching problems and permit obtaining one from the other in linear time for several embedding types [d140435s0p0].
Rooted SPR distance computation uses fixed-parameter-tractable maximum agreement forest (MAF) algorithms as a core method for computing distances between rooted trees [d30106s0p0].
Compression-tree algorithms build directed trees over sensor network nodes to compress correlated sensor data and these algorithms exploit compression-tree structure to achieve near-optimal data collection costs and relate to weakly connected dominating sets for approximation guarantees [d5895s0p0].
Tree edit distance algorithms compute minimum node edit scripts between trees and are applied in biology and intelligent tutoring systems, with dynamic programming used to infer optimal edits and backtracing for edit scripts [d44070s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What specific extremal tree shapes (path, star, broom, balanced tree, caterpillar, Fibonacci tree, etc.) determine worst-case or best-case behavior of common data structures and algorithms—for example binary search trees, AVL/Red‑Black tree rotations, heap array layouts, or union-find trees—and what quantitative performance bounds (height, average search cost, rotation counts) are known for those shapes?

How are inequalities that tie together pairwise distances and subtree multiplicities (e.g., bounds of the form sum_{pairs} d(u,v) ≥ f(subtree counts) or vice versa) employed in concrete domains such as force-directed graph drawing, QSPR/QSAR in chemical graph theory, asymptotic enumeration of labeled/unlabeled trees, or in proofs of isoperimetric-type combinatorial estimates—give specific theorems or papers that apply such bounds?
sub_answers.text:
The replug distance provides a provable lower bound on the unrooted SPR distance and is introduced to enable MAF-style methods for bounding unrooted SPR distance [d30106s0p0].
Tree geometry can be chosen flexibly for tree-Wasserstein constructions because tree geometry does not constrain the richness of the approximation up to the number of edge weights, enabling low-rank approximations of Wasserstein singular vectors via tree-based ground metrics [d102264s0p0].
Asymptotic bounds on diameters of spaces of phylogenetic networks under rearrangement operations (NNI, SPR, TBR) are proven and used to analyse worst-case distances in those spaces [d51414s0p0].
Algebraic constructions relate largest common subtrees and smallest common supertrees and yield linear-time transformations that underlie algebraic relations between subtree containment and supertree composition [d140435s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide a formal graph-theory definition of a binary tree: describe it as an undirected or directed graph, explain the role of a designated root, and distinguish ordered (left/right child) versus unordered rooted binary trees with precise vertex/edge constraints.
sub_answers.text: A rooted tree is a tree with a designated root vertex. [d39061s0p0] A rooted binary tree is a rooted tree in the family of rooted binary n-vertex trees. [d39061s0p0] A balanced binary tree is an instance of a binary tree considered as a special case (denoted BBT) in embedding problems. In a rooted binary tree, define what is meant by a subtree (rooted at a vertex, induced subtree, fringe/subtree versus connected induced subgraph) and state formal counting conventions and formulas for the number of such subtrees (including examples or recurrence relations).

sub_answers.sub_question: Give methods and formulas to compute the Wiener index of a tree incrementally by summing contributions of edges or by using sizes of subtrees on each side of an edge; include the edge-cut pair-count formula W(T)=sum_{e}(s_e*(n-s_e)), descriptions of how to update that sum after adding/removing an edge or moving a leaf, and algorithmic procedures that compute W in O(n) or update in O(1) given subtree sizes.

State combinatorial recurrences and closed-form identities for the number of (induced) subtrees of a rooted binary tree expressed in terms of node degrees and the sizes or subtree-subtree counts of each child (for example, product formulas using counts of subtrees that include the root versus those that do not, recurrences T(v)=f(T(left),T(right), sizes), and generating-function relations), and special-case formulas for full, complete, or degenerate binary trees.
sub_answers.text:
Counts of marked fringe subtrees in large size-conditioned Bienaymé–Galton–Watson trees satisfy a Poisson approximation under microscopic-mark and negligible-clustering conditions [d127320s0p0].
The class of edge-shelling convex geometries of trees is exactly the convex geometry formed by sets of edges of subtrees and is characterized by trace-minimal forbidden minors, with the size of the stem of any rooted circuit equal to two [d6057s0p0].
Subtree substitution treats subtrees with similar semantic functions as exchangeable and yields improved compositional generalization in semantic parsing via data augmentation [d75903s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For standard tree operations (leaf pruning/removal, edge contraction, edge subdivision, rotation as in binary search trees, grafting a subtree onto a new parent, and attaching/detaching a pendant path), give exact formulas or bounds for the change (delta) in the sum of distances (Wiener index) and in the total number of subtrees in terms of n, the sizes of affected subtrees, and pairwise distances; include worked examples showing how to compute the delta from subtree sizes and distance sums.

List known extremal n-vertex tree families and constructions that attain maximum or minimum values for total pairwise distance (Wiener index) and for the number of subtrees (e.g., path, star, caterpillar, complete binary tree, broom/caterpillar variants), and for each family state which metric they extremize, with the relevant asymptotic or exact extremal values and brief statements of the corresponding theorems (for fixed n or fixed maximum degree).

The weighted spanning-tree enumerator of a graph is computable from the determinant of a reduced weighted Laplacian matrix by the Weighted Matrix-Tree Theorem [d49433s0p0].
Linear-algebraic tools such as the Matrix Determinant Lemma and Schur complements can be used to compute weighted spanning-tree enumerators elegantly for several graph families [d49433s0p0].
The mean subtree order μ(G) can decrease when edges are added, and there exist infinitely many pairs of graphs G⊂H with |E(H)|=|E(G)|+1 for which μ(H)<μ(G) [d88200s0p0].
Simple linear-time constructions transform a smallest common supertree to a largest common subtree and vice versa for several embedding types, giving an algebraic relationship between those two problems [d140435s0p0].
